chapter_note: This chapter is overwhelmingly the technical cosmological teaching layer: a stepwise account of how the Father of Life/Living Spirit discharges, gathers, and confines the three dark vessels, leaving measurable residues in the cosmos. The only later material is the dialogue apparatus (“disciples…”, “apostle…”, “enlightener…”) and brief audience-address cues; there is no NT citation and no institutional/pastoral extension.

paragraphs.core_text: When the Father of Life discharged these three vessels from above, they of water and of darkness and of fire, did he perhaps discharge them to their pits at the edge of the firmament? Or did he discharge them first to this earth, and then he swept them from the earth and threw them to their places?
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame formula: “Once again the disciples questioned him, saying to him:”.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Substantive cosmological question (vessels, firmament, pits, earth) is teaching-structural; the Q&A attribution is later hagiographic/frame wrapping.

paragraphs.core_text: when the Father of Life was about to discharge these three vessels he poured the three upon this earth, one by one at its (appointed) hour and season. He discharged them and cast them down to the earth.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue attribution and audience-direction: “Then the apostle says to them: As for what you have asked me about the vessels, you must understand this, that”.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core is impersonal process description (discharge in ordered times/seasons); “apostle” and direct instructional address mark the compilation frame.

paragraphs.core_text: Then he bailed and scooped them from this earth in these three garments, they of wind and of water and of fire, which swathed his body. He poured and made them flow into the three pits [ ... w]hich he had [es]tablished during the construc[tio]n of the worlds [ ... ] they [ ... ] something remained behind on the face of the earth from these three vessels,
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed final audience-directed application clause: “so that you can find their mark and type displayed in the universe.”
paragraphs.temporal_note: The mechanics (garments, pits, construction of worlds, residue) stay within the cosmic system and read as old teaching; the closing “you can find…” is a later didactic gloss addressed to hearers.

paragraphs.core_text: The element that is left in water is the pungency and the salinity of this salty inner sea that surrounds the worlds.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure correspondential residue-teaching (dark remainder → sensory quality; sea surrounding worlds) with no frame or institutional reach.

paragraphs.core_text: And the remnant that is left from the darkness is this black mountain that exists in the surroundings of the sunrise. For when the sun would shine over the world no sunlight is visible there, because the darkness that gushes from it manifests above it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmos→cosmos description: residue of Darkness mapped to a cosmographic feature (black mountain) with an optical effect; no later citation or exhortation.

paragraphs.core_text: And the remnant that remains behind from the fire, upon the earth, are all the mountains and islands from where fumes of fire gush up and are visible. For these things are the remnant of the great vessel, the vestige that was conjoined with this fire that comes up from the earth; together with the mountains and hills [ ... ] places where no fruit sprouts on the trees [ ... ] greater than that place from the limb and [ ... / ... ] the trees shall not bear fruit in that place.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Technical cosmological etiology of volcanic/fire phenomena as residue of the vessel; entirely internal to the system (no institutional/polemical application).

paragraphs.core_text: the vessels that surround the universe, and why they were not discharged from above into the ditches prepared for them (straightaway); but were firstly poured upon the earth, and afterwards were swept from the earth and cast down into their pits?
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame and honorific petition: “Once again his disciples speak to him: We ask you, our master, to [make clear] and instruct us about”.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Underlying content is a structural question about cosmological procedure (surrounding vessels; timing/sequence). The disciple-address and “our master” belong to the later instructional frame.

paragraphs.core_text: When the Father of Life discharged these vessels from above upon the earth, he poured them out for this reason: so that also the water and the darkness and the fire that exist in these three earths would be drawn and ascend towards they that had come down from above, and the earths would be purified and cleansed. Due to this he poured these vessels down to the earth, of water and of darkness and of fire, so that also the water and darkness and fire that exist in the earths would be drawn up towards they that had descended from above.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue attribution and exhortative cue: “Then the enlightener speaks to his disciples: Happen you know this!”.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core causal mechanism (like-to-like attraction; purification of the earths) is systematic cosmology; “enlightener… disciples” is compilation frame and “Happen you know” is didactic address.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, first of all, he discharged the water, the waste, the poison of the rulers who are above. He cleansed the firmaments of the [water ... ] he poured down the dark waters. [Just as the] waters fell from heaven to earth, so also the waters below in the earths were drawn and came up from below towards the waters that had come from above to the earths. The waters [were] purified of the dark poison that exists in them. Then he swept them outside and made them a great vessel and a wall of sea that surrounds the universe, and on which the ships sail.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Sequential technical exposition (first water; firmaments; attraction; purification; formation of encircling sea-vessel) with no frame/pastoral overlay; ships are part of the cosmic architecture here.

paragraphs.core_text: After the water, he discharged the darkness. He purified the firmaments and dried from them the darkness with which they are weighed down. He discharged it down to the earth. Just as he had purified the firmaments, so also he purified the earths. The darkness that is in the earths was drawn up towards the darkness that had been discharged from above. He swept them both out and shut them in that [ ... ] of darkness [ ... / ... ] the water.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second step in a systematic triad (water→darkness→fire): cosmos-internal mechanics of cleansing, drawing-up, and confinement.

paragraphs.core_text: And he discharged the fire from heaven to earth, [ ... at] that time again the fire that was shut [in] the earth below was drawn and came up towards its kind. Fire was added to fire. Afterwards, he swept it out and cast it into the outer underworld, which [he had constructed for] them outside the universe.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Completes the triadic process with the same internal logic (kind-to-kind attraction; sweeping; outer underworld confinement).

paragraphs.core_text: In the same way that he purified the firmaments above as a place for the light-givers to journey [ ... / ... ] so also he purified the earths below and swept from them the fire and the darkness and the water [ ... ] He has purified them for the ascent of these three powers, they of the wind and the water and the fire, which ascend before the Porter and traverse the earths.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal system-closure: purification prepares “light-givers” and the ascent of the three powers; “Porter” functions as a named cosmic office within the architecture, not as an institutional referent.
